title: Fatteh
subtitle: chickpeas, smoky eggplant and brown butter pine nuts
description: A Lebanese-style fatteh of slow-cooked chickpeas topped with charred eggplant, garlicky yoghurt, fried pita and brown butter with pine nuts. Best eaten with a spoon.

steps.text: Drain the chickpeas that were soaked overnight and place in a large pot with plenty of water. Add the bicarbonate soda and 1 teaspoon salt, bring to the boil and cook on low heat for about 3 hours until completely tender. Drain and set aside.
Char the eggplants directly over an open flame for about 5 minutes on each side until blackened and soft. Cool slightly and peel.
Heat oil for deep frying to 180°C. Cut the pita in half crosswise, tear into medium pieces and fry for about 1 minute until browned. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel.
Melt the butter in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer. Add the pine nuts and cook over high heat for about 2 minutes, stirring, until the butter turns brown and the pine nuts are golden.
Divide the chickpeas among four serving plates. Place a whole charred eggplant on each and season with the crushed garlic, lemon juice and salt.

Top with yoghurt, parsley, pomegranate seeds and the fried pita, drizzle with a tablespoon of the brown butter and scatter the pine nuts. Keep the remaining brown butter in a sealed jar in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.
